rationale: To maximize the robot's line-following performance on the held-back track, I designed a balanced geometry with 5 sensors spread evenly across the front to detect the tape line effectively. I chose a moderate sensor size of 0.012 m to balance resolution and coverage. The wheel track is set to 0.14 m for stable turning, with a wheel radius of 0.035 m to allow good speed and torque. The body dimensions are compact but wide enough (0.14 m width, 0.18 m length) to provide stability without risking off-track penalties. Mass is set to 1.0 kg for a good balance between inertia and responsiveness. The controller uses a base speed of 1.5 to push for fast progress while maintaining control. PID gains are tuned with a relatively high proportional gain (kp=12) for responsive steering, moderate integral gain (ki=0.5) to correct steady-state errors, and a derivative gain (kd=3) to damp oscillations. Sensor weights are set symmetrically with negative weights on the right sensors and positive on the left to steer correctly based on line position. The line loss strategy is 'last_direction' to continue searching in the last known direction, minimizing stall time. I expect this design to improve completion rate and reduce line loss events by providing stable, responsive control and good sensing coverage. I request measurements of completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, and steering_oscillation to evaluate performance and control stability.
